description.narrative:
The project contributes to and is aligned to the UN Women “Advancing Women’s Leadership, Empowerment and Resilience in Uganda’s Refugee Response: Phase II” and directly contributes to Outcome 3. The project intends to achieve the following results:
Goal: Positive coping mechanisms and sustainable economic activities are promoted for refugee and host community women and girls.
Outcome 1.0: Refugee and host community women have increased access to sustainable non-agricultural livelihood opportunities.
Output 1.1: Establishment and roll out of savings and lending groups to (105) 3,150 women including digitalisation of savings and linkages to financial institutions such as banks. (10 percent PWDs) -Implemented by OXFAM and URDMC
The 105 women's groups, each with 30 members, engaged in income-generating activities of the Village Savings and Loan Association methodology through engagement with the ENSIBUUKO company for digital VSLA. This will help in the profiling of VSLA and Framers groups, financial linkages, a digital marketplace for farmers, and e-learning through an Android-based smart phone application. These groups will also receive support in the form of tabs or smartphones to aid their saving and financial literacy training and groupdynamics training. Oxfam and its partners will work with the district commercial officer, district community development officer, and office of the prime minister to monitor the groups,minimise related risk, and ensure sustainability once they are matureand have been saving for at least a year.
Output 1.2: Support75 women groups comprising of 2,250 women and youth to establish and manage small and enterprises, support with business and financial skills training including capitalization of businessesand linkages to value addition chains for refugee women through increasingproduction, and support to establish cottage industries and linkages to market opportunities. Implemented by OXFAM

participating-org.narrative:
HISTORY Alice Betty Angwech and Daniel Shamblin founded SEE Impact (Social, Economic, and Environmental Impact) in April 2019, a Ugandan-based social enterprise that aims to reduce poverty through sustainable business solutions based on agroforestry andnatural ecosystem services. They recognized the potential and demand for working with smallholder farmers, refugees, and host communities in Northern Uganda, where farming is the main livelihood for most people and where they face multiple challenges suchas climate change, food insecurity, poverty, and gender inequality. The organisation has gone through several stages and changes since its inception, such as: • Identifying and engaging 300 farmer groups and cooperatives interested in growing tree crops and seed multiplication, collective grain growing, and bulk sale to off-takers. • Establishing a local presence in Northern Uganda, with a field office in Padibe Town Council and a 40-acre satellite farm in Padibe East, Lamwo district. In addition, utilizing the village agency model to reachfarmer groups/cooperatives in other districts within the Acholi Sub-region, namely, Kitgum, Pader, Agago, and Omoro districts, as well as the Lango region and West Nile. • Promoting agroforestry farming practices, which involve the intentional growing of trees and crops together for sustainable livelihood, reduced vulnerability, and environmental protection. Agroforestry has multiple benefits, such as enhancing soil health, diversifying income sources, mitigatingclimate change, and conserving biodiversity. • Providing farmers with quality seeds and seedlings of various crops and trees, such as cashews, soybeans, groundnuts, and mahogany, and helping them access markets and value addition technologies. By doingso, the organisation aims to increase agricultural productivity, create jobs, and improve food security in the region. • Collaborating closely with the district agricultural officers and community development officers for extension services and with theNational Agricultural Research Organisation (NARO) for seed selection and certification processes. • Integrating gender in all its activities, ensuring that women and men have equal access to resources, opportunities, and decision-making. The organization also promotes gender-responsive solutions, such as providing women with fuel-efficient stoves, menstrual hygiene kits, and reproductive health education ACHIEVEMENTS SEE Impact has a strong track record of delivering results and impact in the agribusiness sector. Since 2019, the Company is implementing an equity-funded project “The Farmers Cooperative Development Activity to scale the uptake of Climate Smart Agriculture in Northern Uganda. The project has three components: Component1: Sustainable land management to increase agricultural productivity 2. Adapt and build resilience to climate change 3. Reduce green gas emissions. With a cumulative investment of Three hundred and eighty-five thousand dollars (US$385,000), over four years, (2019to 2023), we successfully reached 12,500 smallholder farmers in Northern Uganda and achieved the following results; • Increasing the average yield of smallholder farmers by 45% and the average income by 50% through adopting climate-smart practices and technologies for the period 2019-2023. • Improving the access to and quality of inputs and markets for smallholder farmers, resulting in a 30%increase in the volume and value of tree seedlings, oil seeds, and cereals produced and sold from 2019 to 2023. • Enhancing the financial inclusion and literacy of smallholder farmers, (SACCOS) leading to a 35% increase in their savings and a 40% increase in consistent membership contributions. 3. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE Mission:
Our Mission: To improve livelihoods,increase resiliency, and advance climate change adaptation in Northern Uganda.
STRATEGIC POSITIONING SEE Impact operates in an environment where smallholderfarmers, refugees, and host communities face multiple challenges such as climate change, foodinsecurity, poverty, and gender inequality. We collaborate with various social actors, including government agencies, business enterprises, civil society organizations, and research institutions, to address these challenges and create opportunities for sustainable development. We play a key role in facilitating dialogue, innovation, and learning among these actors, and in advocating for policies and practices that support the agribusiness sector.
What sets us apart from other organizations is our focus on promoting fast-growing and environmentally friendly tree species as part of our climate-smart and gender-responsive solutions. We have enabled 30 farmer groups (60% women and 40% men) toadopt agroforestry on their farms, which has increased their short-term income sources, with potential future income gains from tree crops and reduced dependency on firewood. These farmers are our direct customers who have supported our business to generate revenues through the purchase of our quality seeds and high-valuetree seedlings. We use different types of trees, such as Mahogany or Casuarina for timber, and fruit and nut trees for food and fodder. We also provide technical assistance, market linkages, and capacity building to our beneficiaries and partners.
